Co-localisation analysis with soft cell type weights

Source: R/colocalisation.R
runColocalisationModels.Rd

Tests, for every pair of leaf cell types and groups, whether the co-localisation of the two differs between the two conditions of an outcome, once with the original labels and once with the bootstrap confidences as soft cell type weights. The co-localisation of each image is the cross-type L-function, computed by spicyR (spicyR::spicy(method = "image")), and relative co-localisation is Statial's Kontextual test (spicyR::kontextualEngine()).

Usage

runColocalisationModels(
  spe,
  cellTypeTree,
  confList,
  outcomeCol,
  r = 50,
  subject = NULL,
  cores = 1,
  parentOverrides = character(0),
  autoOverrideParents = TRUE,
  cellType = "cellType",
  cellID = "cellID",
  imageID = "imageID",
  x = "x",
  y = "y"
)

Arguments

spe

A SummarizedExperiment (e.g. SpatialExperiment) with a cell ID, cell type, image and coordinates for every cell (see getCellData()).

cellTypeTree

A cell type tree, see cellTypeTree.

confList

Confidence list from bootstrapLineageConfidence().

outcomeCol

Name of the colData(spe) column with the per-image outcome. It must have exactly two levels and a single value per image.

r

Radius within which cells count as neighbours, in the units of the coordinates; a single positive number.

subject

Name of the colData(spe) column identifying the subject (for example the patient) each image comes from. With NULL every image is its own subject.

cores

Number of threads.

parentOverrides

Named character vector mapping a to label to the ancestor node (a group, wrapper or lineage in cellTypeTree) that relative co-localisation should compare against instead of the label's own group, for example c("Fibroblast lineage" = "Mesenchymal").

autoOverrideParents

Whether to add overrides found by autoParentOverrides(). Use FALSE to condition only on the parents you list in parentOverrides.

cellType, cellID, imageID

Names of the colData(spe) columns holding each cell's cell type label, a unique cell ID (matching the cellID column of confList), and the image it is in.

x, y

Names of the columns holding the cell coordinates. For a SpatialExperiment whose coordinates are in spatialCoords(), the defaults "x" and "y" refer to its first two coordinates.

Value

A list with the tests modelWeighted, modelUnweighted, modelRelativeWeighted and modelRelativeUnweighted (one row per pair: estimate, the difference for the second level of the outcome compared with the first, its se, statistic, p.value and BH-adjusted p.adj, and for relative co-localisation the parent and side, "attract" or "avoid"), the per-image values weighted, unweighted, relativeWeighted and relativeUnweighted (columns imageID, from, to, colocalisation, and parent for the relative version), and the spicyR results themselves (spicy, a list of weighted, unweighted, relativeWeighted and relativeUnweighted), for spicyR's plotting functions.

Details

Co-localisation of a pair from -> to in an image is the cross-type L-function: how strongly the from cells are attracted to (positive values) or avoid (negative values) the to cells within radius r, with 0 meaning no attraction or repulsion. The area of an image is that of the square around its cells, and cells near the border are edge corrected. Each pair is then tested by a linear model of its per-image values on the outcome (the images are the units); if some subjects have several images, spicyR fits a mixed model with the subject as a random effect instead.

With weights (see confidenceWeights()), a cell of a bootstrapped group belongs to each subtype of the group with its bootstrap confidence: each cell contributes to a label in proportion to its weight, and the density of a label is its summed weight per unit area. With the original labels (weights of 0 and 1) this is the unweighted L-function.

Relative co-localisation compares the co-localisation of from with to to that of from with a parent population of to, so that attraction that only arises because both cell types prefer the same region is not counted. By default the parent of a to cell type is its own group; parentOverrides and autoOverrideParents give broader parents. Pairs whose to has no parent other than itself are not tested.

A label is not paired with itself, nor with a group that contains it.

Examples

# \donttest{
data(lungSubset)
data(lungCellTypeTree)
data(lungConfList)
res = runColocalisationModels(lungSubset, lungCellTypeTree, lungConfList,
    outcomeCol = "disease_status", subject = "subject")
